children: appointed Fabrice Brégier, the former chief executive of Airbus Commercial Aircraft, as chairman of its board as the British electric aircraft developer moves toward certification of its Valo eVTOL aircraft and expands its work in defense and autonomous aviation.

Brégier brings more than three decades of experience across commercial aviation, helicopters, defense and technology. He served as CEO of Airbus Commercial Aircraft from 2012 to 2016 and subsequently as chief operating officer of Airbus Group
and president of Airbus Commercial Aircraft from 2017 to 2018.

Earlier, Brégier was COO of Airbus from 2006 to 2012, where he was involved in the development of the A350 program. He previously served as president and CEO of Eurocopter, now Airbus Helicopters, overseeing its civil and military operations.

His aerospace career also includes a stint at Matra BAe Dynamics and MBDA, where he served as CEO and was involved in multinational defense programs and the integration of several European missile businesses.
More recently, Brégier served as president of Palantir Technologies France
from 2018 through 2024, adding experience in defense, artificial intelligence and data technologies to his aerospace background.
moves from developing and flight-testing its aircraft toward the more complicated stages of certification and commercial deployment.

The company is developing the all-electric Valo, an eVTOL aircraft intended for commercial passenger operations. Vertical says it has also been working on hybrid-electric and autonomous versions of the aircraft platform, potentially broadening its addressable markets beyond conventional electric flight.
Brégier succeeds Ben Story, who had served as interim chairman since May. Story will remain a board member.

The appointment doesn't itself change the company's certification timetable, commercial launch plans or the status of its defense initiatives. Those milestones remain dependent on further testing, regulatory approvals and development work.
